articles.title: Republican leader embarrassed by Ali G film says he plans to sue Sacha Baron Cohen: ‘A liar and a pervert’
articles.summary: Exclusive: Michael Aboud, whose actions in what he believed to be a documentary are likely to come under considerable scrutiny, has expressed anger at the film-maker. • This article contains spoilers for Ali G: Who Iz I?
body: The chair of the El Paso County Republican Party has said he intends to sue Sacha Baron Cohen over footage of the local politician used in new satircal comedy Ali G: Who Iz I?

In the film, Michael Aboud is shown taking part in a training programme with another Cohen character, ex-Mossad terrorist expert Col Erran Morad, who instructs Aboud and fellow Maga sympathisers in self-defence techniques including the wearing, over clothes, of protective plastic buttocks. He also schools them in how to fire bullets from the middle of these buttocks by the repeated up and down manipulation of a rubber penis.

Aboud and a fellow student, former preacher and aspirant actor Joshua Loudermilk, are then recruited by Morad to help in a mission to prevent the birth on US soil of the baby of a fictional South American drugs kingpin, who Mossad has confused for Ali G.

This involves Aboud and Loudermilk helping Morad to abduct Ali G’s girlfriend, Julie (played by the actor Morgana Robinson), while she is apparently in the late stages of labour. They drive her in a kebab van disguised as an ambulance to a remote abandoned medical facility where she gives birth (to a lifelike prosthetic).

articles.title: Ali G: Who Iz I? review – Sacha Baron Cohen’s high-stakes satire punches up and down with spectacular bad taste
articles.summary: Baron Cohen’s live-ammo prankster is back, 20 years on, but has to battle with his own irrelevance in search of big laughs and the approval of a new generation. • Exclusive: Republican leader embarrassed by film says he plays to sue Sacha Baron Cohen: ‘A liar and a pervert’ If you liked Sacha Baron…
body: I f you liked Sacha Baron Cohen’s Ali G the first time around, you’ll like this less; if you disliked it, you’ll dislike this more; if you suspected it was racist, you’ll be more emboldened to say so – especially as Baron Cohen has dreamed up a whole new character apparently to pre-empt and mock precisely that objection. Broad and crass as it often is – in fact always is – this Ali G sequel is sometimes funny: the athletic vigour of our hero’s pranking and punking is like the umpteenth Jackass film at which you might find yourself laughing, and Baron Cohen blunders with the semi-intentional force of an XL bully into the issue of whether jokes are still allowed.

The insurmountable problem is that the film keeps having to tell you who is and isn’t “in on it”: at the beginning, over the closing credits at the end and even briefly in the middle of the action. Well, Ali G was from so very long ago, and even the high-water mark of Baron Cohen’s Borat popularity was quite long ago, and the online media scene now so fragmented that … yes … people have forgotten, a whole new generation doesn’t know. People really don’t recognise him.
points: Baron Cohen’s live-ammo prankster is back, 20 years on, but has to battle with his own irrelevance in search of big laughs and the approval of a new generation.

articles.title: ‘Tangles’ Wins Grand Jury Prize at Animation Is Film Festival
articles.summary: “Tangles” won the Grand Jury Prize at the 9th annual Animation Is Film Festival. Directed by Leah Nelson, the 2-D animated film follows a family impacted by their mother’s battle with dementia.
body: The jury said: “’Iron Boy’ is pure beauty from the medium we all love. Louis Clichy’s ‘Iron Boy’ was an easy stand-out thanks to its beautifully crafted water-color-like and Chinese ink-brush style visuals and how it told a story inspired by the director’s own memories of growing up in rural France. We also admired the way Clichy conveyed a world of emotions with his impressionistic visuals as well as his depiction of a young boy’s personal struggles with a physical handicap and the heartfelt portrayal of a strained father-and-son relationship which avoids sentimentality and the pitfalls of a traditional comic-of-age story.”
“Paper Trail,” directed by Don Hertzfeldt, won the Shorts Jury Grand Prize. The jury described the film as “unique and profoundly moving.”

The Shorts Special Jury Prize went to “Please,” directed by Anna Mantzaris. The jury called it “a wonderfully made, funny, and tender film that captures the absurdity and very human longing for connection.”
points: “Tangles” won the Grand Jury Prize at the 9th annual Animation Is Film Festival.

articles.title: ‘If my brother hadn’t died, my life would be so different’: Olympic boxer Ramla Ali’s incredible journey
articles.summary: From fleeing the Somali civil war to fighting at the Tokyo Olympics, Ali’s life has been remarkable – and now she is being played by Top Boy’s Jasmine Jobson in a new biopic.
body: Boxer Ramla Ali sweeps into the green room of a West End cinema, tiny in a frothy dress with a huge skirt of cascading black feathers. It’s an absolute showstopper. She’s just introduced the premiere of a new film about her life. There are messages on her phone from Bear Grylls and Malala Yousafzai, who are in the audience watching.

But the person who matters most is her mum, who is seeing it for the fourth time. What does she think? “She loves it,” says Ali quietly. The film is In the Shadows, directed by Anthony Wonke and stars Top Boy actor Jasmine Jobson. It tells the story of Ali’s journey to the 2021 Olympics in Tokyo.

And what a journey. Ali was born in Somalia. When she was a baby, her older brother Abdulkadir was killed in an explosion while playing. The family fled Somalia, making the perilous crossing by boat to Kenya, finally arriving in the UK as refugees.
points: From fleeing the Somali civil war to fighting at the Tokyo Olympics, Ali’s life has been remarkable – and now she is being played by Top Boy’s Jasmine Jobson in a new biopic.

articles.title: James Bond Final Screen Tests Are Happening This Week
articles.summary: The crowning of the next James Bond is upon us. Final screen tests for Amazon MGM Studios’ new 007 are set to happen in the next week, sources tell Variety, beginning as early as Friday. Though who exactly will test is up in the air, Callum Turner and Jack Lowden appear to be in the
body: Turner and Lowden have each had their moment in the Bond rumor mill, with Lowden recently moving to the forefront. Speculation reached fever pitch when the Scottish actor’s “Slow Horses” co-star Gary Oldman appeared to suggest that Lowden had made the shortlist. Lowden’s wife, Saoirse Ronan, later weighed in on the buzz, saying that it’s “not really a subject that’s coming up in our house.”

British star Turner was a favorite for the spy earlier this year, with fans even fantasizing about the possibility of a Bond theme song by his wife Dua Lipa. While promoting arthouse film “Rosebush Pruning” at Berlin Film Festival in February, he was immediately asked about the rumors. “It’s very early for that question,” Turner said with a Bond-esque smirk. “I’m not going to comment on it.”

articles.title: ‘Elsinore’ to Receive Gotham Legacy Tribute in Honor of Ian Charleson (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: The Gotham Film & Media Institute will recognize Focus Features’ “Elsinore” with a Gotham Legacy Tribute at the Gotham Film Awards on Nov. 30, honoring the film’s subject, actor Ian Charleson.
body: “Elsinore” tells the story of the Scottish actor who received a devastating AIDS diagnosis at the same time as has the chance to take on the stage role of a lifetime in “Hamlet.”

“’Elsinore’ follows an actor at the height of his powers as he strives to command the stage, facing his own mortality with unflinching honesty, wit, and grace. His final performance becomes his greatest triumph, and a source of healing and inspiration for those around him,” the synopsis reads.

In addition to Scott, “Elsinore” stars Olivia Colman, Billie Piper, Johnny Flynn, and Joe Locke. Colman plays Dr. Margaret Johnson, who treated Charleson and fellow gay men during the HIV epidemic, launching the first-ever dedicated HIV clinic.

“Elsinore” premiered at the Telluride Film Festival and went on to screen in the Special Presentations section at the Toronto International Film Festival, where it received the International People’s Choice Award.

articles.title: Sam Heughan to Star With Viola Davis in Paramount+ Thriller Series ‘Ascent’
articles.summary: “Outlander” star Sam Heughan has been cast to star opposite Viola Davis in Paramount+’s upcoming thriller “Ascent,” set in the world of global corporate crisis and damage control.
body: Yes, there is a bit of coincidental serendipity that Heughan’s character has been paired with a “Catriona.” For eight seasons and 101 episodes of “Outlander,” Heughan starred opposite his similarly named co-star Caitriona Balfe.

“Ascent” comes from Paramount Television Studios, and was created by John Logan (“Skyfall,” “Gladiator”). Logan is showrunner and executive producer, alongside executive producers Michael Aguilar (“Penny Dreadful: City of Angels,” “The Departed”), and Viola Davis and Julius Tennon via their JuVee Productions.
Production on “Ascent” will kick off in Los Angeles in 2027, with an airdate on Paramount+ to be announced later.

As part of “Outlander,” which Heughan also produced, he received award nominations including BAFTA Scotland and Critics’ Choice. His other TV credits include “The Couple Next Door,” “Men in Kilts: A Road Trip with Sam and Graham” and the upcoming “Embassy” with J.K. Simmons and Anna Kendrick. In film, he was seen in “Love Again,” “The Spy Who Dumped Me,” “Bloodshot” and “SAS: Red Notice.”

articles.title: In You Can See Everything, it’s Elizabeth Holmes’s partner who makes for 2026’s timeliest villain
articles.summary: Nathan Fielder’s conversation-igniting film on the Theranos founder finds its darkest moments in her deceptive, Charlie Kirk-loving fiance Billy Evans. Secrets, lies and a shock A-list cameo: how You Can See Everything became the film of the year.
body: This should leave Billy Evans as the odd man out. Evans, Elizabeth Holmes’s partner (she has said they’re not legally married, though they did get engaged in 2018, have two children and seem to treat each other as spouses), is a not-particularly-famous guy whose screen time competes with the other three well-known faces in what is essentially a four-character drama. But while Evans isn’t boxed out in terms of screen time or memorability, he does remain the odd man out in the sense that in all the discussion You Can See Everything has prompted about manipulation, shifting sympathies and who can or cannot be trusted, everyone seems to agree on one crucial point: Billy Evans sucks.

articles.title: Big Brother fans still not happy as housemate called out on behaviour
articles.summary: Ofcom received thousands of complaints related to Omar El Mayer's behaviour in the Big Brother house.
body: A Big Brother housemate who prompted more than 7,000 complaints has been spoken to about his on-screen behaviour - but some fans say the show's not doing enough.
Viewers and women's safety charities had been calling on ITV to intervene in Omar El Mayer and Rhianna Collins' relationship after several heated exchanges between the pair.
He was called into Big Brother's Diary Room during Wednesday's episode and told his language and behaviour "could cause offence". He denied dismissing Rhianna's feelings.
ITV has been contacted for comment. The broadcaster previously said "welfare and safeguarding are prioritised throughout the production".

articles.title: Russell Brand accuser said alleged rape 'really hurt', court hears
articles.summary: The friend of a woman claiming to have been raped by Russell Brand says she said he was "quite aggressive".
body: The friend of a woman claiming to have been raped by Russell Brand told a jury the complainant had told her after the alleged attack that it had "really, really hurt".

The witness who spoke via video link at his trial said she had attended the Hammersmith Apollo theatre in London with the alleged victim in 2009, where they had been invited to the defendant's dressing room after his comedy show.
Statements from the woman's parents were also heard in court, saying their daughter had told them about the alleged attack, and that she had been "very worried about HIV".
Brand, 51, has pleaded not guilty to all seven charges in the trial - three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of indecent assault.

articles.title: House Democrats Want Answers on StubHub CEO’s Ticket Broker Firm: “Conflict of Interest and Potential Grift”
articles.summary: "Eric Baker appears to be using his positions at Andro Capital and StubHub to profit, potentially at the expense of customers, fans, and artists," said Robert Garcia, ranking member of the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
body: StubHub CEO Eric Baker is getting pressed for answers on the executive’s personal ticket broker business, with House Democrats saying Thursday that the dynamic “raises concerns of preferential treatment, abusive practices, and bad deals for concertgoers, sports enthusiasts, artists, and fans.”
The House Democrats had first announced an investigation on the matter back in July, alleging that Baker potentially “engaged in market manipulation and self-dealing.”

In the letter, Garcia asked for descriptions on Andro Capital’s relationship with StubHub, including “cash flow, financing agreements, fees, and related services exchanged between Andro Capital and StubHub.” He gave Baker a deadline of November 5 to respond.
